verses.mystical_translation: A season opens and a scattered people become a single pulse at the holy city.
Leaders and priests raise the place of sacrifice, invoking the covenant law as their guide.
An altar takes its place; ritual steadies trembling hearts with the rhythm of morning and evening offerings.
Under shelters of remembrance, the daily pattern of sacrifice makes time into holy repetition.
Beyond the daily, the cycle of months and fixed feasts gather voluntary devotion into the house of YHWH.
Sacrifice precedes the laying of stones—worship comes before the building is finished.
Money and provisions cross boundaries so timber may carry memory from Lebanon to the shore of rebuilding.
A new year of return organizes labor: age, memory, and community join to bring the holy house into being.
Family lines and clans stand as captains of craft, a human lattice upholding holy work.
Stones are set and music rings—ancient melody consecrates a new beginning.
Unified song names goodness and enduring love; the shout is both memory and vow.
Those who remember the first house are split between tears of loss and cries of hope.
Joy and grief interweave until the single sound reaches far—prophetic noise that carries both mourning and hope.

contemplative_note: Communal rebuilding begins with worship: foundation-laying stirs both tears of memory and shouts of hope; presence and past meet at the altar.
safety_note: Text contains ritual and communal actions; do not weaponize for modern aggression or sectarian claims.
